caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 43 of 1979.
lawyer:
SM Monir, Advocate ----- For the Appellants.
BK Das, Advocate ----- For Respondent No. 1
parties:
Shah Alam and others   ----- Appellants.
Vs.
Masuma Khatoon and others ----- Respondent.
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque, J.: This appeal at the instance of defendant Nos. 1 to 6 and 10 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 17.8.78 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 27 of 1977 decreeing the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title in the 'A' schedule land and recovery of possession in. the 'B' schedule land of the plaint which is part of the 'A' schedule land.

2. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1977 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the 26th, of January, 1977 against appellant Nos. 1-6 as principal defendant Nos. 1 to 6 impleading also appellant No. 7 and respondent Nos. 3-6 as proforma defendant Nos. 7 to 11 in the suit.

3. The case of the plaintiffs in short is that proforma defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali, father of proforma defendant No.8 Ahmmad Ali, proforma defendant No. 10 Alamat Ali and Julmat Ali husband of proforma defendant No.9 Mohammadi Begum, acquired right, title and interest in suit CS plot No. 313 of CS Khatian No. 362 Ext. 5(a) of Mouza Barabo along with other lands on the basis of a deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated the 17th December, 1935 Ext. 1 and A executed in his favour by Jamirjan Bibi and Annabi Bibi, widow and daughter respectively of late Alef and he was in peaceful possession of the said property. While in such title and possession defendant No. 7 transferred entire area of 2.51 acres of suit plot No. 313 to Mohammad Azizur Rahman by a registered deed of sale dated 16th April, 1957 Ext 2 and delivered possession of the said land to the said purchaser. While in such title and possession the said Azizur Rahman transferred eastern half of the suit CS plot No 313 to plaintiff No. 1 Mosammat Masuma Khatoon by a sale deed dated 7th July, 1958 Ext. 2(b) showing the purchased land as Block 'B' in the Map attached to the said sale deed and the western half of the said suit plot No. 313 to plaintiff No. 2 Mosammat Rezia Khatoon by sale deed dated 7th, July, 1958 Ext. 2(a) showing the said land as Block 'A' in the Map attached, to the said sale deed and made over khas possession of said land to the said purchaser plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs got their names mutated with the Government Tahsil office and have been paying rents since 1367 BS and onwards under separate rent receipts Ext. 4 sides. The said CS plot No. 313 has been recorded in the revisional survey operation in six separate plots. As there was wrong recording in respect of the area the plaintiffs fired an application on 25.3.74 Ext. 11 before the Revenue Officer, Dhaka for correction of the said mistake. Since the date of purchase the plaintiffs remained in exclusive khas possession of the suit plot No. 313 measuring an area of 2.51 acres by growing crops therein through their cultivators and bargadars openly, peaceably, and to the knowledge of all persons including the principal defendants and their predecessors-in-interest and of independent right, free from all encumbrances for more than 17 years and by adverse possession too.

4. Further case of the plaintiffs is that the principal defendants who are alleged to be purchasers from proforma defendant Nos. 8 to 10 illegally encroached upon the plaintiffs land and made a small thatched hut towards west of the suit plot No. 313 measuring 8X5 cubits and filled up earth in an area of 0.10 acre and dispossessed the plaintiffs therefrom on 9.2.76 for which plaintiffs lodged a GD Entry No. 491 dated 10.2.76 Ext. 6(a) with Mohammadpur PS. But in spite of repeated requests and demands the said defendants have not vacated the said shed as well as the dispossessed portion fully described in schedule 'B' of the plaint The plaintiffs have been in exclusive possession of the suit plot No. 313 and as such they acquired right, title and interest in the 'A' Schedule property by adverse possession too. The defendants and their predecessors-in-interest have no right, title and interest therein and the principal defendants are liable to be evicted from 'B' schedule of the suit property.

5. The suit was contested by principal defendant Nos. 1 to 6 by filing one joint written statement and by defendant Nos. 8 and 10 by filing another separate statement on identical grounds.

6. Their common case is that the suit is not maintainable in the present form and is bad for defect of party. They also denied the material allegations made in the plaint.

7. Their specific case, in short, is that one Alef was owner of 8.89 acres of land in raiyati jote right in mouza Barabo and the said Alef died leaving his widow Jamirjan Bibi and four daughters, namely, Aliman Bibi, Saliman Bibi, Kctabi Bibi and Annabi Bibi but during the CS operation the said land was recorded in CS Khatian No. 362 Ext. 5(a) wrongly in the name of Jamirjan Bibi alone. Jamirjan Bibi and Annabi Bibi created a Heba-bil-ewaz deed on 17.12.1935 Ext. 1 & A in respect of 3.43 acres of land of CS plot No. 313, 365 and 341 in favour of defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali son of Aliman Bibi. Saliman Bibi also created a Kabala dated 9.2.49 Ext B in respect of 2.60 acres of land of CS plot Nos. 313, 365 and 371 in favour of said Kadam AIi Sirajbi Bibi daughter of Ketabi Bibi sold .73 acre of land out of CS plot No. 313,365 and 371 to Ahmed Ali, Julmat Ali and Alamat Ali defendant Nos. 8 to 10 sons of Kadam Ali by sale deed dated 19.5.47 Ext. B(I) and delivered possession of the same then and there from CS plot No. 313 as per amicable arrangement Sirajbi Bibi by amicable arrangement with other co-sharers had been possessing 1.14 acres of land from the western side of CS plot No. 313 and defendant Nos. 8 to 10 were given possession out of Sirajbi Bibi's 1.14 acres of land from western side of that plot. Kadam Ali had been possessing 1.37 acres of CS plot No. 313 from the eastern side of that plot and he transferred some of his lands to Azizur Rahman who also transferred the same to the plaintiffs. The names of Jamirjan Bibi, Kadam Ali, Ahmed Ali, Julmat Ali, Almat Ali and the plaintiffs were recorded in SA Khatian No. 365 Ext. C(1). Julmat AIi died leaving defendant No.9 Mohammadi Begum and his father defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali as his heirs. Defendant Nos. 8 and 10 sold 0.30 acres of land from CS plot No. 313 to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 by a registered kabala dated 27.7.76 Ext B(2) and delivered possession of the same then and there with their already constructed thatched hut. Defendant No.9 also sold .06 acres of land from said CS plot No. 313 to the defendant Nos. 5 and 6 by a sale deed dated 27.7.76 Ext. B(3) and delivered possession of the same to those purchasers then and there. Thus the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 are in possession of 0.36 acres of land and the defendant Nos. 8 to 10 are in possession of 0.37 acres and the plaintiffs are in possession of 1.37 acres and Sirajbi Bibi is in possession of 0.41 acres of CS plot No. 313 but the present RS record has not been properly prepared and the same is under dispute. The 'A' Schedule property of the plaint is ejmali property of the plaintiffs and the defendants as well as Sirajbi Bibi and as such plaintiffs' suit for declaration of title in the said land and recovery of khas possession from the 'B' schedule land which is part of the 'A' schedule land is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

8. The learned Advocate for the appellants submitted that the land described in 'B' schedule of the plaint is vague and indefinite and on this ground alone plaintiffs' prayer for recovery of possession is liable to be dismissed. He further submitted that Sirajbi Bibi is an admitted co-sharer of the suit holding and on the basis of purchase from her in the year 1947 defendant Nos. 8 and 10 and their brother Julmat Ali became a co-sharer in the suit plot and by purchase from them the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 also became co-sharers in the suit plot with the plaintiffs. As such court below was not justified in declaring title of the suit 'A' schedule property in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs having failed to prove dispossession and the defendants being in possession on the basis of their purchase as well as entry in the SA Khatian they could not be evicted from the suit land.

9. In support of their case plaintiffs examined six (6) PWs including husband of plaintiff No. 2 as PW 1 and their borgader Tyeb Ali as PW 6 apart from documentary evidence Ext. Nos. 1 to l1 Contested defendants also in support of their case examined 4 witnesses including defendants 6 and 10 and also produced and proved documentary evidence Exts. A to E.

10. Is to the vagueness of suit property it is found from description of 'A' schedule to the plaint that the entire area of 2.51 acres of land of CS plot No. 313 of CS Khatian No. 362 of Mouza Barabo with boundaries has been mentioned. In the 'B' Schedule of the plaint the plaintiffs have described dispossessed 0.10 decimals of land to be lying to the west of CS plot No. 313 being the land filled up with earth having a thatched hut measuring 8x5 cubits buict thereon. The learned Advocate of the appellants contends that as there is no mention of boundary of the said decimals of land it is difficult to identify the same. The learned Advocate of the respondents in reply contends that 'though boundaries of the said 0.10 decimals of land have not been mentioned in the plaint no specific objection as to the identity of the said land was either taken in the, written statement or in the cross-examination of the PWs. On consideration of the written statement and the deposition of the witnesses we find that no such objection was taken as to the identity of the suit 'B' schedule land. Therefore we find no merit in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants in this respect.

11. It appears from the deed of Heba-bil-ewaz dated 17.12.35 Ext. 1 executed by Jamirjan Bibi widow of Md. Alef and Anna Bibi daughter of said Md. Alef that they transferred en tire 2.51 acres of land of suit SC plot No. 313 along with other lands to defendant No.7 Kadam Ali and delivered possession of the said land to him . It appears from Ext. 2. deed of sale dated 16.4.57 executed by Kadan Ali in favour of Md. Azizur Rahman that he transferred the entire 2.51 acres of land of suit plot No. 313 to the said purchaser for valuable consideration and delivered possession of the said land to him. It also appears from Ext. 2(a) sale deed dated 7.7.58 that the said Md. Azizur Rahman transferred western half of the said CS plot No. 313 to the plaintiff No. 2 Mosammat Rezia Khatoon and delivered possession to her in the block 'A' shown in the Map attached to the sale deed. Similarly from Ext. 2(6) it appears that the said Md. Azizur Rahman transferred eastern! half of suit CS plot No. 313 to plaintiff No. 1 Masuma Khatoon and delivered possession of the said land to her from Block 'B' of the map attached to the said deed defendant on the other hand claimed that Sirajbi Bibi was 10 possession of 1.14 acres of land from the western side of CS plot No. 313 and while in such possession by sale deed Ext B(1) dated 19.5.47 she transferred 0.73 acres of land out of CS plot Nos. 313, 365 and 371 to defendants 8, 10 and Julmat Ali husband of defendant No. 9 and delivered possession of the said land to the said purchasers from western side of CS plot No. 313 only. But neither in the recital nor in the schedule of the said kabala there is any mention that the said purchasers were given possession in the said 0.73 acres or from the western part of suit CS plot No. 313 alone. In view of the same the Claim of the said defendants 8 and 10 that they got possession in the said purchased land from the western side of suit CS Plot No. 313 is control to the recital of the said document and the oral evidence adduced by the defendants Contrary to the said recital cannot be relied on and rightly rejected by the trial Court. To reconcile the said defendants at the trial adduced evidence contrary to their claim as made out in paragraph No. 19(d) of the when statement that after purchase on the basis of the said deed dated 19.5.47 they got possession in their purchased land from the western side of suit CS plot No. 313 on the basis of amicable arrangement with their father Kadam Ali. This shows Kadam Ali had been in sole, possession of the suit plot No. 313. Moreover, Kadam Ali admitted in sale deed dated 16.4.57 Ext. 2 that he transferred the entire 2.51 acres of land of suit plot No.313 to Md. Azizur Rahman vendor of the plaintiffs and delivered possession to him who in his turn sold the same to the plaintiffs by sale deeds dated 7.7.58 Ext. 2(a) and 2(b) and delivered possession thereof to them. Thus oral evidence from the defendants side that Kadam Ali delivered possession of 0.73 acre of land to his sons defendants 8 and 10 and Julmat Ali by way of amicable partition after their purchase from Siraji Bibi is negatived by such admission of Kadam Ali in the said sale deed Ext. 2 There is no evidence that defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali has any strained relationship with his sons, and we find no explanation why he was not examined by the defendants in support of the contention that they got possession from him. This shows Kadam Ali was not willing to support the defendant. Rather documentary evidence discussed above clearly shows that Kadam Ali was in sole possession of entire land of suit plot No. 313 till his transfer to Azizur Rahman in 1957.

12. The appellant Nos. 1-6 have filed an application for amendment of paragraph No. 19(d) of the written statement filed by them as defendant Nos. 1-6 and also to add a new paragraph No. 19(i) in the said written statement the middle portion of the said paragraph No. 19(d) full stop after the words "as per amicable arrangement" is sought to be deleted and the words between Kadam Ali and his sons defendants 8,10 and Julmat Ali is sought to be added after the said full stop. It is also sought to be added in the new paragraph 19 if that Title Suit No. 501 of 1978 has been filed by Sirajbi Bibi in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for partition of the entire lands of CS Khatian No. 362 of mouza Barabo and subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 812 of 1985 of the Second Court of Subordinate Judge: Dhaka and the same is still pending. The learned Advocate for the respondents vehemently opposed this prayer for amendment on the ground that it is an afterthought to make their inadmissible evidence as admissible, We have already found earlier that the claim of the defendants that defendants 8, 10 and Julmat Ali got possession in their purchased land on the basis of amicable arrangement with their father Kadam Ali cannot be relied upon. Moreover, as pointed out by Mr. BK Das, the learned Advocate for the respondents that the said partition suit is no longer pending, rather it was decreed by the trial Court and on appeal by his clients the said decree was reversed by this court in First Appeal No. 843 of 1991. In view of the above, we find no merit in the said application for amendment of the written statement of defendant Nos. 1-6. Moreover, even if we allow this amendment the unamended written statement of defendant Nos.8 and 10 will remain intact in paragraph No. 19 (d) in the very same language as in paragraph No. 19 (d) of the written statement of defendant Nos. 1-6. They being mere subsequent purchasers from defendant Nos. 8 to 10 cannot make a contradictory claim with their vendors. Therefore, the application for amendment is rejected.

13. Now coming to the evidence of possession of the plaintiffs it is seen that PW 1 Syed Nuruddin Wahed Ali, husband of plaintiff No.2 has deposed in support of the plaintiffs' exclusive possession of the suit plot. He stated that the plaintiffs possessed the suit plot through their borgader Sultan Mia who at a subsequent stage executed a borga kabuliyat Ext. 3 in their favour and after him plaintiffs possessed through their borgader PW 6 Md. Tayeb Ali who executed borga Kabuliyat Exts. 3(a) to 3(c). He further stated that the plaintiffs paid rent from 1367 BS up to 1386 BS by mutating their names vide rent receipts Ext. 4 series. PW 1 is corroborated in respect of plaintiffs exclusive possession of the suit plot by a neighboring resident PW 2 Azharul Islam who is a retired Government servant. PW 6 Md. Tayeb Ali also corroborated the PW 1. PW 3 Mansur Ali who had a piece of land to the north of the suit plot and which he sold 8/9 years before and who is a resident of the locality stated that he saw Kadam Ali to possess the entire suit plot and defendant No. 1 had been possessing 10 or 11 decimals in the suit plot by sing a hut for the last 2 and 2½ years and prior to that PW 1 and his bhaira possessed the entire suit plot and the defendants did not possess any portion of the suit plot prior to 2 or 2½ years of course he stated in cross-examination that he saw sons of Kadam Ali to possess along with their father without stating the time. It must be before his sale of the land to Azizur Rahman. It is but natural for the sons to help their father in cultivatting the land. That does not mean their independent possession and the same is clear from his denial of defendants suggestion that the plaintiffs possessed 4½ pakhis in the east and the rest 1.14 acre in the west in the suit pot. PW 4, Kazi Fakhruddin Ahmed, a retired government servant and a surveyor measured the suit plot and prepared the map attached to plaintiffs' Kabalas Ext. 2(a) and 2(b) on the identification of husband of plaintiff No. 1. PW 5 Lal Mia who resides 500 feet away from the suit plot clearly stated in his deposition that he saw Kadam Ali to possess the entire suit plot. 'He further stated that while.in possession Kadam Ali sold it to one Azizur Rahman who sold to the plaintiffs who possessed through Sultan and at present Tyeb Ali has been possessing on plaintiffs behalf. But this witness also stated that 5/6 years after purchase by the plaintiffs sons of Kadam Ali possessed some portion in the western part of the plot. Relying upon this the learned Advocate for the appellants strenuously contended that the defendants Sifo and Julmat Ali possessed from western part of the suit plot as claimed by them on the basis of amicable arrangement with Kadam Ali From the cross-examination of DW 1 Almat Ali defendant No. 10) it is seen that the defendants 8 and 10 received compensation for 0.24 acres of land of plot No. 371 of their kabala land in LA case No. 41 of 1964-65 in which case plot Nos. 365 and 371 were acquired. This goes to show that PW 5 meant to say that sons of Kadam Ali were in possession in the land of plot No. 371 and not in the suit plot. This portion of the deposition of PW 5 inconsistent with his earlier statement in his deposition appears to us not to have been correctly recorded Almat Ali is defendant No. 10 and ow 3 Sirajul Huq son-in-law of Kadam Ali is defendant No.6. He also attested the sale deed executed' by Kadam Ali in favour of Azizur Rahman vendor' of the plaintiffs. They being interested in the result of the suit they cannot be relied upon without 'independent corroboration. DW 2 Haji Kala Chand Mia who claims to be a resident of Agargaon and an old man of 95 years is an over zealous witness. He stated that defendant No. 10 was 40 years-old at the time of Kabala Ext. B(1) whereas defendant No. 10 himself as OW 1 admitted that he was only 14/15 years old at 'that time. He also stated that defendant No. 1 is a Municipal Commissioner but denied the suggestion that he came to depose falsely to please him DW 4 Ali Mia who also claims to be a resident of Agargaon is another over zealous witness. He stated that Kadam Ali sold the eastern part and still owned western part of the suit plot though he stated on recall that he did not say that Kadam Ali possesses the western portion still now. How could sons of Kadam Ali possess their entire purchased 0.73 acres from plot No: 313 as deposed by DWs when as admitted by DW 1 that they received compensation for requisition and acquisition of plot No. 371? The statement of the Dws. that defendant Nos. 8,10 and Julmat Ali constructed the straw hut is belied by the recital in the kabalas Ext. B(2) and B(3) in favour of principal defendant Nos. 1-6 inasmuch as there is no mention of such straw hut in the said deeds. Therefore, it is difficult to rely upon the testimony of the said DWs contrary to recital in their sale deeds. In view of the above discussion of evidence record we are of the view that Kadam Ali had been in sole possession of the suit plot No. 313 till his sale in 1957 to Mohammad Azizur Rahman vendor of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs got possession from him of the said land after their purchase in 1958 and the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the entire suit plot till their dispossession of the 'B' schedule land measuring 0'10 acres on 9.2.76.

<u>14. The learned Advocate for the appellants relied on the decision in the case Abdul Jalil Sikder and others Vs. Khorshed Ali Dakua and others reported in 27 DLR (AD) 143 and in the case of Hazera Begum and others Vs. Rousan Ara Begum and others reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22 and contended that even if the plaintiffs are found to have been in sole possession of the suit plot No. 313 that will not amount to ouster of the co-sharer defendants however long their possession might be and title of the defendants, will not be extinguished in the suit plot by such possession of the plaintiffs and as such, court below was wholly wrong in declaring title of the plaintiffs in the entire land of suit plot No. 313. It is true that defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali being a descendant of the original owner and his sons also similarly being transferees from a descendant of the original owner sole possession of Kadam Ali could not have extinguished the title of his co-sharer sons. But the plaintiffs being strangers to the family and they having purchased from Azizur Rahman transferee of Kadam Ali and having got exclusive possession to the knowledge of the defendants and having mutated and recorded their name in assertion of their title denying title of sons of Kadam Ali and paid rents from the time of their purchase continuously in spite of objection by the sons of Kadam Ali their open possession is a notorious fact and nothing but ouster of the sons of Kadam Ali from the suit plot. Even if we accept defence case that sons of Kadam Ali also possessed the suit plot with their father as deposed by PW 3 fact remains that the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the suit plot for 16 years as already found by us and this leads to the irresistible conclusion of their ouster from the suit plot. It may be noted that SA Khatian Ext. 5 prepared by merely revising the CS Khatian and recording names of sons of Kadam Alialong with the names of the plaintiffs even without omitting name of CS recorded tenant Jamirjan Bibi and the government acquired plots has no presumptive value and we find up merit in the contention of the appellants that they have interest in the suit property on the basis of the said SA Khatian. Moreover, it is pointed out by the learned Advocate for the respondents that in the judgment of FA No. 843 of 1991 between the same parties it has been found that corrected RS Khatian in respect of the suit plot was finally published in the name of the plaintiffs subsequent to the SA Khatian. Since the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the entire land of CS plot No. 313 openly, notoriously and continuously for more than 16 years beyond the statutory period of limitation, right, title and interest if any of the sons of Kadam Ali in that plot had been extinguished by adverse possession before the alleged dispossession of the plaintiffs from the 'B' schedule land. Facts of the above decisions are distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case and as such principle enunciated in those cases are of no help to the appellants.</u>

<u>15. When a co-sharer in sole possession transfers the land in his possession to a stranger to the family and such purchaser possesses the land in assertion of his title to the exclusion of other co-sharers of his vendor openly, notoriously and continuously denying title of such co-sharers by mutating and recording his name in the record of rights and paying rent separately the same will amount to ouster of such co-sharers and such possession for more than 12 years will extinguish title of such co-sharers by adverse possession.</u>

16. As to the grievance that actual dispossession of the plaintiffs from the 'B' schedule land has not been proved by evidence it is seen from Ext. 6(a) a copy of GD Entry No. 491 dated 10.2.76 that the plaintiffs complained against defendant No. 1 Shah Alam that he with the help of defendant Nos. 8-10 and 20/25 others forcibly trespassed and constructed a dochala thatched hut on 9.2.79 in the suit plot and attempting to cultivate the land. The said defendant No. 1 has not denied the said allegation. He appears to be owner of a Textile Mills. He being a rich man felt shy to depose falsely appearing before the court. DW 2 also indirectly supported the plaintiffs case of such dispossession by saying that about 2½ years ago defendant Nos. 8 and 10 repaired the straw hut. Kabala Ext. B(2) in favour of defendant Nos. 1-4 executed on 21.4.76 shows that defendant No. 1 purchased 0.11 acre of land and this also supports plaintiffs case. We therefore, find no merit in the contention that the plaintiffs failed to prove actual dispossession for the 'B' schedule property. We, therefore, find no merit in this appeal.

In the result, the appeal is dismissed with cost and the judgment and decree of the court below is affirmed.

End.
